fmt/Device_DeclaredIsTooLongFor: "{0}" is too long for the QuadStick to load, so nothing was written. A profile name can be {1} characters at most, counting ".csv", and this one is {2}. Shorten the name in cell A2 and install again.
fmt/Device_FileNameIsNoLongerOn: {0} is no longer on the device. Refresh the list and try again.
fmt/Device_FileNameIsProtectedAndCannot: {0} is protected and cannot be deleted. Removing it can leave the device unusable.
fmt/Device_NameIsNotAPlain: "{0}" is not a plain file name the QuadStick can hold, so nothing was written. Change cell A2 to a simple name like "mygame.csv".
fmt/Device_OnlyAPlainFileName: Only a plain file name on the device root can be deleted, not a path.
fmt/Device_RefusingToOverwriteDefaultCsv: Refusing to overwrite default.csv without explicit confirmation. A wrong default.csv can disable flash-drive access.
fmt/Device_RefusingToOverwritePrefsCsv: Refusing to overwrite prefs.csv without explicit confirmation. prefs.csv holds device-wide settings, and a wrong one can leave the QuadStick unusable.
fmt/Device_ThatFileIsNotDirectly: That file is not directly on the device root, so it was not deleted.
fmt/Device_ThatFolderDoesNotLook: That folder does not look like a QuadStick drive (no default.csv at its root). Pick the USB volume that appears when the device is plugged in.
fmt/Device_TheQuadStickWasDisconnectedWh: The QuadStick was disconnected while {0} was being written. Your previous version is safe at {1}. Plug the device back in, check whether {2} is still on it, and install again.
fmt/Device_ThisProfileHasValidationError: This profile has validation errors and cannot be installed:
fmt/Device_WritingFailedMidSwapAnd: Writing failed mid-swap and {0} could not be put back on the QuadStick. Your previous version is safe at {1}. Copy it onto the device by hand.
fmt/Device_WritingFailedMidSwapThe: Writing failed mid-swap; the previous version of {0} was restored from backup. The device is unchanged.
fmt/Fn_1LatchesTheOutputOn: 1 latches the output on. Anything above 1 is how long the press lasts.
fmt/Fn_FiresOnceYourInputIs: Fires once your input is at least this strong.
fmt/Fn_FiresWhileYourInputStays: Fires while your input stays under this strength.
fmt/Fn_HoldTheInputLongerThan: Hold the input longer than this and the output latches on instead of tapping.
fmt/Fn_HoldsTheFirstTapThis: Holds the first tap this long before the rapid-fire starts.
fmt/Fn_HowFarDownTheAnalog: How far down the analog output moves each time.
fmt/Fn_HowFarUpTheAnalog: How far up the analog output moves each time.
fmt/Fn_HowFastItTapsWhile: How fast it taps while you hold the input.
fmt/Fn_HowLongTheTapPresses: How long the tap presses for. 1 latches the output on instead.
fmt/Fn_HowManyPressesOneActivation: How many presses one activation sends.
fmt/Fn_KeepsSteppingThisOftenWhile: Keeps stepping this often while you hold the input.
fmt/Fn_KeepsTheOutputPressedThis: Keeps the output pressed this long after you let go.
fmt/Fn_LetGoInsideThisWindow: Let go inside this window and it counts as a tap. Hold longer and nothing fires.
fmt/Fn_StopsFiringAgainOnceYour: Stops firing again once your input goes past this, so the two numbers make a band.
fmt/Fn_TheOnAndOffCycle: The on-and-off cycle length at full strength. Softer input stretches it.
fmt/Fn_WaitsThisLongAfterYou: Waits this long after you activate, then presses.
fmt/Fn_WaitsThisLongBeforeReleasing: Waits this long before releasing the other row's latched output.
fmt/Issue_0UsedToMeanNo: 0 used to mean no dead zone at all, and firmware from 2025 substitutes 129 raw counts instead, so the stick gains a small dead zone this file never asked for
fmt/Issue_5WasPCOnlyNo: 5 was "PC only, no joystick" until 2025 and is the Nintendo Switch Pro Controller now, so an updated QuadStick shows up to the console or PC as a different controller entirely
fmt/Issue_ADirectionSettingLeftAt: (A {0} setting left at 0 uses the shared sip_puff_ value instead.)
fmt/Issue_APercentOver100Is: . A percent over 100 is a level no input reaches, so this row never fires.
fmt/Issue_ArgsIHasADecimal: "{0}" has a decimal part. The device reads whole numbers only, so it acts as "{1}".
fmt/Issue_ArgsIIsLargerThan: "{0}" is larger than {1}, the device's limit for the first parameter; it overflows into the second parameter.
fmt/Issue_ArgsIIsNegativeThe: "{0}" is negative; the device does not handle negative parameters predictably.
fmt/Issue_ArgsIIsNotA: "{0}" is not a number. Parameters to "{1}" must be whole numbers, and the device reads this one as 0.
fmt/Issue_BActionNameHasNoButton: "{0}" has no button behind it yet, so this row does nothing on the QuadStick.
fmt/Issue_BOutputHasNoValue: "{0}" has no value in column B, so the device reads it as 0.
fmt/Issue_BOutputIsADevice: "{0}" is a device setting and the device reads its value from column C, which is empty here. Column B is skipped, so this row may set the value to 0.
fmt/Issue_BOutputIsADevice2: "{0}" is a device setting but no value follows it, so the device sets it to 0.
fmt/Issue_BOutputIsALegacy: "{0}" is a legacy output name: the firmware knows it but the current official list does not include it.
fmt/Issue_BOutputIsNotA: "{0}" is not a documented output name (PlayStation or XBox convention).
fmt/Issue_BluetoothOnlyKeyboardRow: This mode is on "{0}", and it has {1} mouse or keyboard row, on row {2}. Firmware from 2025 or newer only sends mouse and keyboard over USB when the channel includes USB, so over a cable that row does nothing while the gamepad half of the mode keeps working. Older firmware sent them anyway.
